source_name: MNB Statisztika – Publikációs témák (statistics topic index)
why_relevant: Master index of every MNB statistical publication theme (payment data, supervisory statistics, financial institutions' balance sheets, methodologies). Use it to discover datasets not surfaced by search.

source_name: MNB – A nyílt bankoláshoz kapcsolódó pénzforgalmi szolgáltatók és harmadik fél szolgáltatók adatai (open banking / PSD2 TPP data)
why_relevant: Consolidated MNB-maintained directory of ASPSPs and registered third-party providers (AISP/PISP/CISP) with API and contact details. Directly names Hungarian open-banking fintechs (e.g. KBOSS.hu, Billingo, Nyíltbankolás Zrt., Aggreg8) that are potential partners, competitors or channel players for payments vendors.

source_name: MNB Piaci szereplők keresése (hub page for all registers)
why_relevant: Hub page that enumerates every MNB register: general institution search, intermediaries (közvetítők) search, special databases, and cross-border activity lists. Single best entry point to discover which registers exist at all.

source_name: MNB Hungarian cross-border service providers list (EN)
why_relevant: English-language MNB list of Hungarian payment institutions and e-money institutions passporting services cross-border. Identifies which Hungarian PSPs operate regionally — relevant for competitor footprint mapping beyond HU.

source_name: Portfolio Banking Technology – historical editions archive (2017–2025)
why_relevant: Prior-year editions remain online with their own program/speaker/sponsor pages (2017, 2019, 2020, 2022, 2023, 2024 seen in results), giving a ~9-year longitudinal series of which vendors sponsored Hungarian banking IT and which bank executives shared a stage with which supplier. The 2019 participant list already names 4iG Nyrt., ACI Worldwide, Accenture Kft., adesso Hungary.

source_name: Portfolio Banking Technology conference — programme, speakers and sponsors
why_relevant: The annual Hungarian banking-IT conference. Sponsor lists and speaker affiliations are an efficient census of who is actively selling to Hungarian banks in a given year, and joint bank+vendor sessions effectively announce live accounts.

source_name: Portfolio.hu Banking Technology conference programme & bank/vendor interviews
why_relevant: The conference agenda is effectively a public roster of which bank IT executives are presenting alongside which vendors — an annual, structured snapshot of active bank–supplier relationships that no press room states outright.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – Tagjaink (Hungarian Banking Association member list)
why_relevant: Canonical enumeration of the Hungarian credit-institution universe (~60-70 entries: banks, mortgage banks, branches of foreign banks, plus associated members/observers such as GIRO Zrt., KELER, BISZ, Magyar Államkincstár, OBA and sector sub-associations). Single best seed list for the banking actor map and for snowballing to each bank's own site.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – Munkacsoportok (working groups)
why_relevant: Working-group roster reveals where the sector's technical agenda sits: Bankkártya munkacsoport (cards), Pénzforgalmi (PAD) + SEPA munkacsoport, Készpénzforgalmi munkacsoport, Digitalizációs munkacsoport, Treasury. Names the topics banks are jointly solving — a leading indicator of upcoming procurement/tender themes in payments and digital channels.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség (Hungarian Banking Association) – member directory & press releases
why_relevant: GIRO is an association member; the association's member list, working-group outputs and press releases map the institutional actors and signal collective infrastructure projects (instant payments, fraud data sharing) before vendor selection.

source_name: Company registry aggregators (OPTEN, Céginfo, Nemzeti Cégtár, CompanyWall, EMIS)
why_relevant: Fast lookup of ownership, cégjegyzékszám, activity codes, credit ratings and management for every actor in the cell (Grepton, CARDNET, Sysdata, Netlock etc.), including ownership changes that signal consolidation among bank-serving integrators.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf Kft. (Hungary) - company filings and profile aggregators
why_relevant: Hungarian company registry aggregators (Nemzeti Cégtár, OPTEN, iCégtár, Kompass) expose revenue, headcount, ownership and even won-tender lists for local subsidiaries of self-service hardware vendors. Lets the competitive field for SCO/ATM/kiosk in HU be sized from filings rather than press claims; the same method applies to NCR Voyix, Toshiba GCS, Laurel and local integrators.

source_name: TED CPV vocabulary reference (Fő és kiegészítő közös közbeszerzési szójegyzék)
why_relevant: Authoritative bilingual CPV code list; gives the exact Hungarian label for each code so queries and downstream classification use the official term rather than a guess. Essential to build the checklist-free CPV slice for this cell.

source_name: Céginformációs Szolgálat (Ministry of Justice) – institutional hub page
why_relevant: Master pointer to every official HU company-data channel: free company information, filing submission (OBR), bulk dataset sales, direct company announcements, and the legal basis for each. Best single page to re-check when portals move or rules change.

source_name: MKIK 'Vállalkozz digitálisan' accredited IT supplier and product catalogue
why_relevant: Chamber-of-commerce accredited supplier registry listing Hungarian IT vendors and their approved products (Grepton appears there). A vetted, structured list for enumerating and validating local integrators.

source_name: FinTechZone — Elektronikus fizetési megoldások kézikönyve (handbook)
why_relevant: A curated Hungarian directory of electronic payment solutions and providers — effectively a pre-built actor map of the HU PSP/acquiring landscape, ideal seed for glossary and entity resolution.

source_name: GIRO Zrt. – beszállítói szerződések közzététele (supplier contract disclosure PDF)
why_relevant: Line-by-line register of GIRO Zrt.'s supplier contracts (megrendelo/szallito, date, subject) under the Hungarian 'uvegzseb' transparency rule. This is the single highest-value primary vendor list for the Hungarian clearing/instant-payment infrastructure operator: it names IT suppliers (e.g. Cardinal Kft., R&R Software, C-NET Informatikai) with contract dates.

source_name: Hungarian Fintech Association (HFA / hunfintech.com) member directory
why_relevant: Membership list is a ready-made actor map of Hungarian fintech and bank-tech vendors (Dorsum among them), useful for snowballing beyond the obvious integrators into niche ISVs competing for bank budget.

source_name: IVSZ – Digitális Vállalkozások Szövetsége, tagvállalatok directory
why_relevant: The largest Hungarian ICT-supplier directory (~19 pages of members, several hundred companies), filterable by size tagozat (Mikro/KKV/Nagyvállalati/Multi/Társult) and sector tagozat (Informatikai, Digitális, Startup és Scale-up, Telekommunikációs). This is the primary way to enumerate small local IT integrators and software houses that serve banks but never surface in English-language search.

source_name: BankWeb.hu banki állás section
why_relevant: Sector-specific HU portal aggregating 'banki állás' links; a cheap pointer to the full set of HU bank career pages, including smaller institutions (savings banks, MFB, Gránit, Magnet) that mainstream enumeration misses.

source_name: Mesterséges Intelligencia Koalíció – alapító tagok jegyzéke (Digitális Jólét Program)
why_relevant: A published, numbered founder-member roster of the national AI Coalition — a cross-sector list mixing banks, telcos, IT integrators and universities in one PDF. Coalition rosters like this are the classic 'small local players invisible to search' harvest, and AI working groups are where bank-side automation vendors self-identify.

source_name: AppsRunTheWorld customer database — ACI Worldwide BASE24
why_relevant: Lists named institutions running a specific payment product (BASE24), broken out by country. A cheap way to hypothesise which Hungarian banks run ACI switching before confirming against vendor press releases.

source_name: ATM Marketplace — Diebold Nixdorf company showcase (news + resources)
why_relevant: Vendor-sponsored showcase pages republish ATM vendor case studies, white papers and deployment news in one place, including NCR/Atleos corporate-structure coverage. Useful pointer into vendor collateral that is otherwise buried behind gated resource centres.

source_name: Az Év Honlapja (Website of the Year) – winners archive
why_relevant: Hungary's main digital/web award with a per-year winners archive that regularly includes finance-category entries; entries are usually submitted by the agency or implementation partner alongside the bank, so the winners list doubles as a bank↔digital-supplier partnership register. Purely professional recognition (no cash prize), so entries reflect real vendor marketing intent.

source_name: BKIK – Budapesti Kereskedelmi és Iparkamara, tagozatok / osztályok
why_relevant: Budapest chamber is where most financial-sector suppliers are seated. Its sectional structure includes a Gazdasági Szolgáltatások Tagozat with an Általános Pénzügyi Szolgáltatás Osztály — a ready-made segmentation of financial-services firms in the capital, plus event and committee listings that name active companies.

source_name: Blockchain Magyarország Egyesület – Magyar Blockchain Térkép
why_relevant: An explicit, published MAP of Hungarian blockchain/DLT actors — the association curates the ecosystem rather than just its own members. Founding member of the Blockchain Koalíció, consortium member of the DigitalTech EDIH, and affiliated to INATBA, so its pages also link outward to coalition rosters and EU digital-innovation-hub partner lists.

source_name: Budapest Fintech Week (HFA + Startup Hungary) – partner/sponsor roster
why_relevant: Community-organised Hungarian fintech week (2025 edition 4–5 Dec, KPMG Conference Center Budapest) whose named collaborators are themselves a partnership disclosure: Hungarian Fintech Association, Startup Hungary, Ergomania, HOLD Fund Management, KPMG Hungary, Visa and CIB Bank. Shows which bank and card-scheme money backs the local fintech community.

source_name: Company/ecosystem databases with Hungary filters (F6S, ensun, Dealroom, CB Insights)
why_relevant: Structured English-language listings of Hungarian fintech companies and of bank-affiliated investors (e.g. MKB Fintechlab, the incubator tied to what is now the MBH Bank group). Chiefly valuable as an actor-discovery pointer to feed back into media searches; company-count claims are unreliable.

source_name: Cégjegyzék.hu – index of free and paid Hungarian company-data services
why_relevant: Curated pointer page comparing the Hungarian cégadat-lekérdezés landscape (free vs paid channels). Useful for periodically re-discovering new or renamed aggregators in this cell.

entity_name: Diebold Nixdorf investor press-release CDN archive
source_name: Diebold Nixdorf investor press-release CDN archive (q4cdn)
why_relevant: Diebold Nixdorf's IR document store holds the raw press-release files (e.g. bank99 ATM-as-a-Service, 2025 awards). Contract announcements naming a Hungarian bank would land here; the file store is easier to sweep than the marketing site.

source_name: Digitális Kereskedelmi Szövetség (DKSZ)
why_relevant: Newer digital-commerce alliance whose named participants include Mastercard, Google, DHL Express, PwC, IVSZ, Growww Digital, Boxy and Oander — i.e. it directly documents a card-scheme/consultancy/e-commerce partnership cluster. Its academies and mentor programmes surface which vendors are educating Hungarian merchants (a proxy for go-to-market pushes).

source_name: FeaturedCustomers — vendor customer-reference aggregator
why_relevant: Aggregates published customer references, testimonials and case studies per vendor (Diebold Nixdorf profile seen with 39 references). Fast way to enumerate a vendor's named install base and spot any Hungarian entity without crawling each vendor site.

entity_name: Felelős Fintech Tartalmakért pályázat és díj
source_name: Felelős Fintech Tartalmakért pályázat és díj – díjazottak
why_relevant: Dedicated Hungarian fintech award with a published winners page; smaller than Év Bankja but surfaces niche fintech and content/communication actors that larger awards miss. Useful for completing the long tail of the HU fintech actor map.

source_name: HUNGEXPO / Sirha Budapest – exhibitor directory (kiállítói lista)
why_relevant: Hungary's main trade-fair operator publishes a structured, searchable exhibitor list per fair. Sirha Budapest (HORECA/food) is the fair where POS terminals, cash registers (pénztárgép) and merchant payment acceptance vendors exhibit to the merchant side rather than the bank side — i.e. the acquiring/merchant-services channel that banking conferences miss. Same directory pattern applies to other HUNGEXPO fairs.

source_name: HVCA – Magyar Kockázati- és Magántőke Egyesület, Tagok
why_relevant: ~70 members (28 full, 32 associate, 10 individual) categorised by role, incl. an /category/investors view listing fund managers (Hiventures, FundWise, Impact Ventures, Integral Venture Partners, Hodler). Associate members are typically the law/advisory/tech service layer. Identifies who funds Hungarian fintechs — funding events are the earliest signal of a new competitor or an emerging partner.

source_name: IPAR 4.0 Nemzeti Technológiai Platform – tagszervezetek
why_relevant: A cross-sector national technology platform whose member list includes associations themselves (IVSZ is listed) alongside companies and research institutes. Platform/cluster rosters like this are second-order pointers: they enumerate the associations to sweep, and catch industrial-IT suppliers who also sell to financial back offices.

source_name: K-Monitor adatbázis (public-money watchdog, tagged by organisation)
why_relevant: NGO-curated index of press articles and documents tagged by contracting authority and company (e.g. a dedicated KEF tag). Excellent pointer layer: surfaces the deals that got journalistic scrutiny, and thereby names actors and contract nicknames you can then look up in the primary registers.

source_name: KELER Zrt. – contract register file (sensenet document API)
why_relevant: Appears to be the machine-served contract-disclosure table (Szerződés azonosító / dátum / megnevezés) behind KELER's transparency page; search extraction surfaced named IT suppliers (SLASH Szoftverfejlesztő, ROUTOLOGIC, Cardinal, DataCare Rendszerintegrációs, ÁBRIS Informatikai, SmartX Solutions) tied to the KELER Szolgáltatásfejlesztési Program (KSZP).

source_name: Kozadat.hu közadatkereső (public data / institution registry)
why_relevant: Aggregator that maps Hungarian public institutions to their statutory disclosure pages, including contract registers. Good snowballing entry point to find the disclosure URL of hospitals, transport operators and utilities in this cell.

source_name: Magyar Faktoring Szövetség
why_relevant: Founded 2003; members are banks and specialised financial institutions active in factoring — a receivables-finance niche where fintech entrants (Flexibill, Péntech) and bank incumbents compete directly. Statutes and about pages name the constituent institutions; cooperation agreement with the Leasing Association links the two rosters.

source_name: Magyar Lízingszövetség – tagok és pártoló tagok
why_relevant: 36 member asset-financing companies (leasing arms of banks + independent financial enterprises) and, crucially, a separate 'Pártoló tagok' (supporting members) page that lists their SERVICE PROVIDERS — e.g. BISZ Központi Hitelinformációs Zrt., CallTec Consulting. Supporting-member lists are the cleanest association-side view of who supplies technology and BPO to lenders. Also an associated member of Bankszövetség.

source_name: Magyar Nemzeti Kereskedelmi Szövetség (MNKSZ) – Tagjaink
why_relevant: Retail-trade association with an explicit member page and a standing e-kereskedelem topic area. Retailers are the acceptance side of payments (POS terminals, online cash registers, instant-payment acceptance obligations), so this roster identifies the buyer universe for payment-acceptance vendors.

source_name: MarketResearch.com — Hungary banking/cards report aggregator
why_relevant: Reseller catalogue that enumerates which publishers have Hungary-specific banking, cards and payments reports and when they were refreshed — an efficient way to discover analyst houses covering Hungary without querying each one, and to detect new report releases.

source_name: Nemzeti Jogszabálytár / Jogtár – Kbt. and 424/2017 (XII.19.) Korm. rendelet on e-procurement
why_relevant: Defines what MUST be published, where, in what form and within what deadline — i.e. the legal guarantee behind this whole cell, plus the exemptions (in-house, defence/security, central-bank secrecy) that predict the blind spots in the award record.

source_name: Neumann János Nonprofit Kft. (NTP) – project portfolio
why_relevant: Ministry background institution running national data-economy and digitalisation programmes (NATUK and successors) largely on EU funds; its project list reveals state-driven digital initiatives and partner ecosystems adjacent to payments and digital identity.

source_name: Nevogate / paymentgateway.hu partner integration directory
why_relevant: A Hungarian payment-gateway aggregator listing which acquirers and payment methods it integrates (Worldline/SIX, PayU, SEPA DD, etc.) — an indirect but concrete map of who is technically connectable in the HU market.

source_name: NJSZT – Neumann János Számítógéptudományi Társaság, szervezeti és támogatói tagság
why_relevant: The oldest Hungarian ICT professional society; its corporate/supporting membership page plus a high-frequency newsletter enumerate IT companies, research groups and universities. Complements IVSZ by capturing the academic-industrial and legacy-systems side (including banking-IT veterans) rather than the commercial-lobby side.

source_name: Open Contracting Partnership Data Registry — Hungary / TED publications
why_relevant: Registry describing what procurement data exists for Hungary and the EU, in what format, with what coverage and update cadence. A pointer source that reveals additional publishers and OCDS endpoints we would not find by direct search.

source_name: openprocurements.com Hungary - CPV-indexed procurement browser
why_relevant: Third-party index of Hungarian procurement notices organised by CPV code (e.g. 51214000 parking-meter installation services). Useful for discovering the right CPV codes for kiosks, ticket machines, POS terminals and cash-handling equipment, which then makes EKR/TED searching far more complete.

source_name: Research and Markets — Mordor and multi-publisher Hungary listings
why_relevant: Second large report reseller; its publisher pages and country filters surface Hungary payments/POS/banking titles from many houses, with abstracts that often disclose segment definitions and named vendors.

source_name: Shoprenter / Számlázz.hu integration directories
why_relevant: Dominant Hungarian webshop and invoicing platforms publish which PSPs are integrated; their directories and blog guides are a bottom-up census of which acquirers/PSPs actually reach Hungarian SME merchants.

source_name: SimplePay technical-partner / developer pages
why_relevant: Publishes the list of integrated technical partners (webshop engines, ERPs, POS vendors) — an actor map of the HU e-commerce/payments integration ecosystem, effectively a partnership registry.

source_name: Területi kereskedelmi és iparkamarák – regisztrált vállalkozói adatbázisok (county chamber company databases)
why_relevant: Each county chamber republishes its own filterable registered-company database (county, city, activity, name) and business partner-search pages. These regional cuts surface small local IT/POS service firms outside Budapest that neither IVSZ nor fintech associations list.

source_name: Thales Cyber & Digital (cpl.thalesgroup.com) — payment HSM resources
why_relevant: payShield product and resource pages carry integration guides, partner listings and occasional named case studies; the partner/integration lists are the realistic route to identifying who supplies HSMs into Hungarian issuers and processors, since Thales rarely names individual banks.

entity_name: Visa Global Registry of Service Providers
source_name: Visa Global Registry of Service Providers
why_relevant: Searchable registry of Visa-registered/validated service providers (processors, gateways, personalisation, hosting). Filtering by country surfaces providers serving the Hungarian market and their validated service categories — a direct competitor/vendor map for payments infrastructure services.
